summary: 'How are you' is HOW followed by a point to YOU, with raised eyebrows. It's the standard follow-up to hello.
steps: Sign HOW: two bent hands, knuckles touching, that roll open so the palms face up.
Point to the person for YOU.
Raise your eyebrows and hold them until they answer. That's what makes it a question.
note: Common answers are FINE, GOOD, OK, or TIRED, usually with a point to yourself first. The face carries most of the real answer.
mistakes: Flat eyebrows. Without them this reads as a statement.
Rolling HOW only halfway. The hands finish palm-up.

faq.q: How do I answer 'how are you' in ASL?
faq.a: Point to yourself, then sign a feeling: FINE, GOOD, TIRED, HAPPY. The clips for I'M-FINE and I'M-GOOD are on their own pages.
